newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa shares seen up next week after dreary run.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa shares seen up next week after dreary run.

text.p: South African shares are seen stronger next week as investors grow weary of the market's recent lethargy and stocks play catch-up with Wall Street's net gains this week, analysts said on Friday.
Although the Johannesburg Stock Exchange has generally been taking its cue from the Dow, it has lagged the strength of the U.S. bourse.
"The market has been very lethargic and should start rising. The Dow has been rising and we have to catch up," said Greg Amoils, a portfolio manager at Irish Menell Rosenberg.
Market analysts said the JSE appeared to be suffering from a lack of direction with some viewing a cut in interest rates as the best remedy to pull it out of the doldrums.
"A rate cut has got to happen. (The high rate) is strangling the market," Amoils said.

Although market expectations of a cut in rates in the second half of the year were dealt a blow by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals when he hinted last month that monetary policy might still need to be tightened, a number of institutions have begun talking again of lower rates.

On Monday banking group Investec said rates should fall by some two percentage points in 1997 although real rates would remain high. Financial services giant Sanlam last week also predicted two one-point cuts still likely in the second half.
Poor company earnings reports from a number of leading South African firms have weighed on the market this week.

These include retail firm Edgars Ltd which posted its first slide in annual earnings year in a decade and construction firm Pretoria Portland Cement Ltd which reported results below analysts' expectations.
"Here you have two of the big companies in their sectors coming out and saying things are not all that good out there," said Johan Marais, a director at Societe General Frankel Pollak.
However, not all earnings reports were negative.
"We have seen some good ones like Reggies and Didata," Amoils said.

A number of key firms report next week, including banking group Nedcor Ltd, which is expected to show robust earnings growth, and beer giant South African Breweries Ltd seen with a modest 14 percent rise in profits.
Packaging company Nampak Ltd and timber firm Hunt Leuchars & Hepburn also report.
Gold shares, which analysts said were treated with caution this week, were seen moving sideways in the week ahead.
"Anything exciting that happens to the gold price is quickly reversed and (shares) are left in tatters," Amoils said.
Matt Brenzel, portfolio manager at Coronation Asset Management said the gold price had good upward potential, if it was not for gold sales by Europe's central banks.
He said a recent report by analysts from Goldfields Ltd indicated that there was good demand for gold, while the supply side, particularly from South Africa, was weak.
"So assuming that the central bank keeps its feet out of the market the gold price is at bottom," he said.
The market will also look to the producer price inflation figure due next week.
